comparison: Both evaluate binding affinity claims (C3, C4, C40-C43). OpenEval finds the data well-supported across multiple assays. Peer reviewers raise critical methodological concerns about SDS-PAGE for oligomerization assessment and potential avidity artifacts in affinity measurements, suggesting use of monomeric Fab. OpenEval rates SUPPORTED while peer rates UNCERTAIN due to these technical issues.

Both evaluate epitope mapping claims (C6, C44-C51). OpenEval finds comprehensive support from docking, mutagenesis, and binding studies. Peer reviewers acknowledge compelling evidence for specific residues but note the data are not conclusive for NPC1 binding site targeting, relying on competitive binding with MR78 for approximate localization. OpenEval rates SUPPORTED while peer rates UNCERTAIN due to incomplete epitope definition.

Both evaluate neutralization claims (C5, C54-C58, C85). OpenEval finds data supported but notes limitation of pseudovirus rather than authentic virus. Peer reviewers explicitly state 'convincing binding to Marburgvirus GP and neutralization of Marburg viruses by AF03' with improved Figure 3 presentation. Both rate SUPPORTED, though OpenEval emphasizes the pseudovirus limitation.

OpenEval R4 evaluates in vivo protection (C59-C62, C86, C93) while peer R3 covers both neutralization and in vivo data. OpenEval finds bioluminescence data supported but emphasizes pseudovirus limitation. Peer reviewers accept the findings without raising concerns about the protection data. Both rate SUPPORTED.

Both evaluate cleaved GP neutralization claims (C7, C64-C66, C89-C90). OpenEval finds differential neutralization statistically significant but questions biological relevance of artificial enzymatic cleavage. Peer reviewers state 'convincing neutralization of Ebolaviruses by AF03-NL' with improved Figure 4 presentation. OpenEval rates SUPPORTED with caveats while peer rates SUPPORTED without reservations.

Both evaluate CI-MPR-dependent internalization claims (C67-C71). OpenEval finds multiple complementary assays consistently support the mechanism. Peer reviewers note FACS data quality limitations but find cell staining data in Figure 5C compelling. Both rate SUPPORTED despite minor data quality concerns.

OpenEval R7 evaluates broad-spectrum neutralization (C72-C75, C97) while peer R6 evaluates mechanism validation (C8, C72, C74-C80). OpenEval finds neutralization data robust but mechanistic explanation speculative. Peer reviewers find control experiments in Figure 7 compelling for the internalization mechanism. Both rate SUPPORTED, with overlapping claims on neutralization breadth.

Both evaluate CI-MPR mechanism validation (C76-C80). OpenEval finds gain/loss-of-function experiments provide strong mechanistic evidence. Peer reviewers state the data 'support the internalisation and stabilisation mechanism' with compelling control experiments. Both rate SUPPORTED with strong agreement on mechanistic validation.

Both address C97 regarding weaker GP binding by AF03-NL. OpenEval notes this paradox with stronger neutralization and finds the mechanistic explanation speculative. Peer reviewers accept this finding without question as it supports the internalization mechanism interpretation. Both rate SUPPORTED.

OpenEval evaluates background claims about filoviruses (C1-C2, C9-C20, C81-C82) as established knowledge with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these contextual claims.

OpenEval evaluates structural and mechanistic background claims (C21-C36) as established knowledge with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these contextual claims.
OpenEval evaluates MARV therapeutic development context (C37-C38, C83-C84) as accurately representing the literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background claims.
OpenEval evaluates established knowledge claims (C52, C88) justifying experimental design choices. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these contextual claims.

OpenEval evaluates speculative future application claims (C91, C92, C94) as UNCERTAIN, noting need for authentic virus validation and additional models. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these forward-looking claims.
OpenEval evaluates negative control claim (C98) as appropriate validation for the assay system. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this methodological control.
